newsitem.title: INDIA: India shares end down, TELCO seen up after results.
newsitem.headline: India shares end down, TELCO seen up after results.

text.p: Indian shares closed broadly lower on Tuesday after an early rally attracted profit-booking, traders said.
Market action was focussed on India's leading truckmaker Tata Engineering & Locomotive Company (TELCO) ahead of its 1996/97 (April-March) results which were released after markets closed.

TELCO beat market expectations when it announced a whopping 44 percent increase in net profit for the year ended March 31, 1997. The firm said net profit surged to 7.62 billion rupees in 1996/97 (April-March), from 5.3 billion in the previous year.
"It's a brilliant result on the face of it," said Anupam Thareja, analyst at HSBC B&K Securities.
TELCO shares jumped 11 rupees, or nearly three percent, to 404 in after-hours kerb deals in Bombay. The stock had closed 7.0 rupees lower at 393 in official trade at the Bombay bourse.
Automobile analysts -- who had pegged their 1996/97 net profit forecasts at around 7.2 billion rupees -- said a lower tax rate had boosted profits.
"The key area I had underestimated was taxation," said K.N. Sreenivasan, automobile analyst at Jardine Fleming India Broking. "I had assumed the tax rate to be around 29 percent."
